decisions.reason: Grounds attribution in symptom-log.txt and contrast-probe.txt: same file, divergent readers (file-trace RPC fine vs sidebar tab failing) rules out disk/FS/renderer, and meta.status 'none' is correctly read as metadata never arriving, localizing the fault to the workspace-files Remote/provider RPC chain; notes the host row is declared but static presence/activation is unproven, without demanding an unseen internal function.

Uses combo-probe.txt to validate the 62/62 per-module sweep and reject the ~4–5 KB joined URL as a request-format artifact that must never be cited as missing modules; explains the real loader fetches the roster's per-entry (bounded) URLs and never synthesizes one giant join, without needing the 3 KB constant.

Separates the dsh-paste-input fold warnings as an independent display-time parse bug in a different plugin, and uses boot-manifest-excerpt.txt to explain the textpreview→documentpreview rename and session-only canOpen, correctly tying that scope to the outside/absolute claim failure only, not the session tab's stalled metadata read.

Orders restart first, then rollback to the #5999-verified 0.1.3-alpha.2 escape hatch (explicitly rejecting staying on alpha.1), then upstream; explicitly rejects plugin rewrite/retry/fallback as masking a host-chain gap, and treats the prior alpha.1 roster mismatch as prior-round history while establishing via Probe 3 that alpha.2 modules all serve, so no missing-bytes claim.

Lists complete upstream forensics (version pair, profile provenance, roster/census, valid sweep, same-file contrast with meta.status, console/host logs, Remote network trace, session root resolution) and proposes named boot diagnostics: roster/serving self-probe, gateway handler liveness check for advertised Remotes, and an end-to-end read smoke, plus a client-side timeout surfacing for 'none' status.

caps.reason: The report explicitly rejects the joined-URL 404 as a measurement and concludes static serving is healthy with all 62 modules served individually.
The report affirmatively rejects plugin rewrite, retry, fallback, and any duplicate service insertion, placing the fix on the host/upstream side.
